newsitem.title: USA: Fixed-rate mortgages jump in week - FHLMC.
newsitem.headline: Fixed-rate mortgages jump in week - FHLMC.

text.p: Rates on fixed-rate home mortgages jumped in the week ending Jan. 10, but edged lower for adjustable loans, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.
Thirty-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 7.85 percent in the week, up from 7.67 percent the previous week, while 15-year loans climbed to 7.35 percent from 7.18 percent.
But adjustable mortgage rates inched down to an average of 5.54 percent from 5.56 percent.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.08 percent, the 15-year 6.59 percent, and the adjustable loan 5.45 percent.
"Mortgage rates followed the capital markets upward on news that the economy is stronger than expected, once again raising fears of inflation," said Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist.

"The employment report due out tomorrow will influence next week's mortgage rate figures," Van Order added. "If this report supports indications of strong economic growth, we will see interest rates rise even further."
On Friday the Labour Department will issue December employment data. Earlier Thursday it said that producer prices rose 0.5 percent last month.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average of 1.8 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans in the week, both up from 1.7 percent the previous week. They charged 1.4 percent on adjustable loans, unchanged from last week.
